 PASSED IN MVC NO.138/2015, ON THE FILE OF THE Madhu vs R Sundaramoorthy on 23 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/145260069/
1  ADDITIONAL SENIOR CIVIL JUDGE AND CHIEF JUDICIAL  MAGISTRATE, TUMAKURU, PARTLY ALLOWING THE CLAIM  -2-  MFA No. 7520 of 2018 PETITION FOR COMPENSATION AND SEEKING ENHANCEMENT OF COMPENSATION.
 THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR ADMISSION, THIS DAY,
THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT 1.
The claimant, being dis-satisfied with the compensation of Rs.2,02,908/- awarded by the Tribunal, is in appeal.
2. The fact that the accident occurred and the further fact that the offending vehicle was insured is not in dispute.
3. The Tribunal, on an analysis of the medical evidence, has concluded that the claimant has suffered permanent disability to the extent of 10% to the whole body.
4. The Tribunal has determined the monthly income, notionally at Rs.6,120/-.

Since there is no credible documentary evidence to ascertain the actual monthly income, it would be appropriate and prudent to adopt the monthly income determined by Karnataka State Legal Services Authority,
which for the accident of the year 2014, would be Rs.8,500/-.
5. As the claimant was aged 24 years, a multiplier of '18' would have to be applied.

Consequently, the claimant would be entitled to a sum of Rs.1,83,600/- (Rs.8,500/- x 12 x '18' x 10%) towards 'loss of future income'.
6.
The Tribunal has awarded Rs.10,000/- towards 'pain and sufferings' which is meagre and the same is enhanced to Rs.40,000/-.

7. The Tribunal has noticed that the claimant had produced medical bills to the tune of Rs.65,890/-,
but yet it has awarded only Rs.58,716/-.
In the light of the medical bills produced, it would be appropriate to award a sum of Rs.65,890/- towards 'medical expenses'.
8. The Tribunal has awarded Rs.2,000/- towards 'loss of amenities, attendant charges, nutrition and diet'.

In my view, having regard to the percentage of disability, it would be appropriate to award a sum of Rs.40,000/- towards 'loss of amenities' and Rs.15,000/- towards 'conveyance, nutrition and attendant charges'.

Madhu vs R Sundaramoorthy on 23 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/145260069/
2 9.
The Tribunal has not awarded any income towards 'loss of income during laid-up period'.
Having regard to the nature of injuries sustained, it would be appropriate to treat the laid-up period as two months and award a sum of Rs.17,000/- under the said head.
10. Consequently, the award of the Tribunal is modified and the following sums are awarded as compensation :

Sl. Particulars Amount Amount  awarded by awarded by  No.
 Tribunal this Court  (Rs.) (Rs.)
 1. Pain and sufferings 10,000/- 40,000/-
 2. Medical expenses 58,716/- 65,890/-
 3. Loss of future income 1,32,192/- 1,83,600/-
 4. Loss of amenities, 2,000/- 40,000/-
 nutrition, diet and  attendant charges  5. Conveyance, nutrition NIL 15,000/-
 and attendant charges  6. Loss of income during NIL 17,000/-
 laid-up period  Total 2,02,908/- 3,61,490/-
11.
Thus, the claimant is held entitled to the total compensation of Rs.3,61,490/- as against Rs.2,02,908/- along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till its realization.
12. The Insurance Company is directed to deposit the amount of compensation awarded within two months from the date of receipt of a certified copy of this judgment.

3 13.
On such deposit, the claimant is entitled to withdraw the same as per the terms of the award of the Tribunal.
14. The appeal is accordingly allowed in part.
